# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Analisis
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

EDAD_MINIMA_H = 48  # los videos mas nuevos no entran en comparaciones de vistas
N_MINIMO = 8        # por debajo de esto un grupo se marca como muestra chica
RE_EMOJI = re.compile(
    "[\U0001F000-\U0001FAFF☀-➿⬀-⯿️‍]")
RE_PALABRA = re.compile(r"[A-Za-zÀ-ɏ0-9']+")


def med(xs):
    xs = [x for x in xs if x is not None]
    return statistics.median(xs) if xs else None


def fmt(x, dec=2):
    if x is None:
        return "s/d"
    if isinstance(x, float) and dec == 0:
        return f"{x:,.0f}".replace(",", ".")
    if isinstance(x, float):
        return f"{x:.{dec}f}".replace(".", ",")
    return f"{x:,}".replace(",", ".")


def tabla(titulo, cabecera, filas):
    print(f"\n### {titulo}\n")
    print("| " + " | ".join(cabecera) + " |")
    print("|" + "---|" * len(cabecera))
    for f in filas:
        print("| " + " | ".join(str(c) for c in f) + " |")


def marca(n):
    return f"{n}" if n >= N_MINIMO else f"{n} (muestra chica)"


def spearman(xs, ys):
    def rangos(v):
        orden = sorted(range(len(v)), key=lambda i: v[i])
        r = [0.0] * len(v)
        i = 0
        while i < len(orden):
            j = i
            while j + 1 < len(orden) and v[orden[j + 1]] == v[orden[i]]:
                j += 1
            for k in range(i, j + 1):
                r[orden[k]] = (i + j) / 2 + 1
            i = j + 1
        return r
    if len(xs) < 5:
        return None
    rx, ry = rangos(xs), rangos(ys)
    mx, my = statistics.mean(rx), statistics.mean(ry)
    num = sum((a - mx) * (b - my) for a, b in zip(rx, ry))
    den = (sum((a - mx) ** 2 for a in rx) * sum((b - my) ** 2 for b in ry))
    return num / den ** 0.5 if den else None


def limpiar_titulo(t):
    """Titulo sin hashtags ni emojis, para contar palabras."""
    t = RE_HASHTAG.sub("", t)
    t = RE_EMOJI.sub("", t)
    return " ".join(t.split())


def cargar():
    with CSV_SALIDA.open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
        filas = list(csv.DictReader(f))
    for r in filas:
        for k in ("duracion_s", "vistas", "me_gusta", "n_hashtags",
                  "n_etiquetas", "n_doblajes_auto", "posicion"):
            r[k] = int(r[k]) if r[k] not in ("", None) else None
        r["pub"] = datetime.strptime(
            r["publicado_utc"], "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"
        ).replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
        cap = datetime.fromisoformat(r["capturado_utc"])
        r["edad_h"] = (cap - r["pub"]).total_seconds() / 3600
        r["maduro"] = r["edad_h"] >= EDAD_MINIMA_H
        limpio = limpiar_titulo(r["titulo"])
        r["titulo_limpio"] = limpio
        palabras = RE_PALABRA.findall(limpio)
        r["palabras"] = palabras
        r["n_palabras"] = len(palabras)
        r["n_car"] = len(r["titulo"])
        mayus = [p for p in palabras
                 if len(p) >= 2 and p.isupper() and any(c.isalpha() for c in p)]
        r["n_mayus"] = len(mayus)
        letras = [c for c in limpio if c.isalpha()]
        r["todo_mayus"] = bool(letras) and all(c.isupper() for c in letras)
        r["emoji"] = bool(RE_EMOJI.search(r["titulo"]))
        r["pub_col"] = r["pub"] - timedelta(hours=5)
    # indice relativo: vistas / mediana del propio canal (solo maduros)
    por_canal = defaultdict(list)
    for r in filas:
        por_canal[r["canal"]].append(r)
    for canal, rs in por_canal.items():
        m = med([r["vistas"] for r in rs if r["maduro"]])
        for r in rs:
            r["indice"] = (r["vistas"] / m) if (m and r["maduro"]) else None
    return filas, por_canal


def grupo_indice(filas, clave, orden=None):
    """Mediana del indice relativo por grupo. Devuelve filas de tabla."""
    g = defaultdict(list)
    for r in filas:
        if r["indice"] is not None:
            k = clave(r)
            if k is not None:
                g[k].append(r["indice"])
    llaves = orden if orden else sorted(g)
    out = []
    for k in llaves:
        v = g.get(k, [])
        if not v:
            continue
        sobre = sum(1 for x in v if x >= 2) / len(v) * 100
        out.append((k, marca(len(v)), fmt(med(v)), f"{sobre:.0f} %"))
    return out


CAB_IND = ["Grupo", "n", "Mediana del índice", "Con índice de 2 o más"]


def tramo_palabras(r):
    n = r["n_palabras"]
    if n <= 2:
        return "1 a 2 palabras"
    if n <= 4:
        return "3 a 4 palabras"
    if n <= 7:
        return "5 a 7 palabras"
    if n <= 10:
        return "8 a 10 palabras"
    return "11 o más palabras"


ORD_PAL = ["1 a 2 palabras", "3 a 4 palabras", "5 a 7 palabras",
           "8 a 10 palabras", "11 o más palabras"]


def tramo_dur(r):
    d = r["duracion_s"]
    if d is None:
        return None
    for tope, nombre in ((60, "hasta 59 s"), (90, "60 a 89 s"),
                         (120, "90 a 119 s"), (150, "120 a 149 s")):
        if d < tope:
            return nombre
    return "150 a 185 s"


ORD_DUR = ["hasta 59 s", "60 a 89 s", "90 a 119 s", "120 a 149 s",
           "150 a 185 s"]


def franja(h):
    ini = h // 3 * 3
    return f"{ini:02d} a {ini + 2:02d} h"


def analizar() -> None:
    filas, por_canal = cargar()
    nombres = [c[0] for c in CANALES if c[0] in por_canal]
    en = [r for r in filas if r["idioma_canal"] == "en"]
    es = [r for r in filas if r["idioma_canal"] == "es"]
    formato_en = [r for r in en if r["grupo"] != "vecino"]
    maduros = [r for r in filas if r["maduro"]]
    print(f"Filas: {len(filas)}; maduras (>= {EDAD_MINIMA_H} h): "
          f"{len(maduros)}; en inglés: {len(en)}; en español: {len(es)}")
    print("Índice = vistas del video / mediana de vistas de los videos "
          "maduros del mismo canal.")

    # 1. Resumen por canal
    t = []
    for c in nombres:
        rs = por_canal[c]
        mad = [r for r in rs if r["maduro"]]
        fechas = sorted(r["pub"] for r in rs)
        dias = max((fechas[-1] - fechas[0]).total_seconds() / 86400, 0.01)
        t.append((c, len(rs), len(mad),
                  fechas[0].strftime("%m-%d") + " a "
                  + fechas[-1].strftime("%m-%d"),
                  fmt(float(med([r["vistas"] for r in mad]) or 0), 0),
                  fmt(float(med([r["duracion_s"] for r in rs])), 0),
                  fmt((len(rs) - 1) / dias, 1)))
    tabla("Resumen por canal",
          ["Canal", "n", "n maduros", "Rango de fechas (UTC)",
           "Mediana de vistas (maduros)", "Mediana de duración (s)",
           "Videos por día"], t)

    # 2. Forma del titulo por canal
    t = []
    for c in nombres:
        rs = por_canal[c]
        n = len(rs)
        t.append((c, n,
                  fmt(float(med([r["n_palabras"] for r in rs])), 0),
                  fmt(float(med([r["n_car"] for r in rs])), 0),
                  f"{sum(1 for r in rs if r['n_mayus']) / n * 100:.0f} %",
                  f"{sum(1 for r in rs if r['todo_mayus']) / n * 100:.0f} %",
                  f"{sum(1 for r in rs if r['emoji']) / n * 100:.0f} %",
                  f"{sum(1 for r in rs if r['hashtags_titulo']) / n * 100:.0f} %"))
    tabla("Forma del título por canal",
          ["Canal", "n", "Mediana de palabras", "Mediana de caracteres",
           "Con palabra en MAYÚSCULAS", "Todo en mayúsculas", "Con emoji",
           "Con hashtag en el título"], t)

    # 3. Longitud del titulo frente al indice
    tabla("Palabras del título frente al índice (canales en inglés del "
          "formato)", CAB_IND, grupo_indice(formato_en, tramo_palabras, ORD_PAL))
    tabla("Palabras del título frente al índice (canales en español)",
          CAB_IND, grupo_indice(es, tramo_palabras, ORD_PAL))
    t = []
    for c in nombres:
        mad = [r for r in por_canal[c] if r["maduro"]]
        if len(mad) < 8:
            continue
        orden = sorted(mad, key=lambda r: -r["vistas"])
        k = max(len(orden) // 4, 1)
        top, resto = orden[:k], orden[k:]
        rho = spearman([r["n_palabras"] for r in mad],
                       [r["vistas"] for r in mad])
        t.append((c, len(mad), k,
                  fmt(float(med([r["n_palabras"] for r in top])), 1),
                  fmt(float(med([r["n_palabras"] for r in resto])), 1),
                  fmt(float(med([r["n_car"] for r in top])), 0),
                  fmt(float(med([r["n_car"] for r in resto])), 0),
                  fmt(rho)))
    tabla("Cuartil superior de vistas frente al resto, por canal",
          ["Canal", "n maduros", "n cuartil superior",
           "Palabras (cuartil superior)", "Palabras (resto)",
           "Caracteres (cuartil superior)", "Caracteres (resto)",
           "Spearman palabras y vistas"], t)

    # 4. Mayusculas y emoji
    def caps(r):
        if r["todo_mayus"]:
            return "todo en mayúsculas"
        return "con palabra en MAYÚSCULAS" if r["n_mayus"] else "sin mayúsculas"
    tabla("Mayúsculas frente al índice (inglés, formato)", CAB_IND,

    tabla("Mayúsculas frente al índice (español)", CAB_IND,

    tabla("Emoji en el título frente al índice (todos)", CAB_IND,

    # 5. Palabras iniciales
    for nombre, sub in (("inglés, formato", formato_en), ("español", es),

        for r in sub:
            if not r["palabras"]:

                c1[(k, ini)] += 1
                if r["indice"] is not None:

        t = [(f"{ini}", k, n, marca(len(ind[(k, ini)])),

             for (k, ini), n in c1.most_common(40) if n >= 4]
        tabla(f"Arranques de título más frecuentes ({nombre}, "

    # 6. Hashtags

                  f"{max(r['n_hashtags'] for r in rs)}",
                  f"{sum(1 for r in rs if '#shorts' in (r['hashtags_descripcion'] + ' ' + r['hashtags_titulo']).lower().split()) / len(rs) * 100:.0f} %",
                  ", ".join(f"{h} ({n})" for h, n in cnt.most_common(6))))
    tabla("Hashtags por canal",

    tabla("Número de hashtags frente al índice (todos)", CAB_IND,

                       "1 a 3" if r["n_hashtags"] <= 3 else
                       "4 a 5" if r["n_hashtags"] <= 5 else "6 o más",
                       ["0", "1 a 3", "4 a 5", "6 o más"]))

    # 7. Descripcion, etiquetas, categoria, idioma, doblaje, fijado
    t = []
    for c in nombres:
        rs = por_canal[c]
        n = len(rs)
        sin_h = [len(RE_HASHTAG.sub("", r["descripcion"]).strip()) for r in rs]
        fij = Counter(r["comentario_fijado"] for r in rs)
        t.append((c, n,
                  fmt(float(med([len(r["descripcion"]) for r in rs])), 0),
                  f"{sum(1 for x in sin_h if x > 0) / n * 100:.0f} %",
                  fmt(float(med([r["n_etiquetas"] for r in rs])), 0),
                  ", ".join(f"{k} ({v})" for k, v in
                            Counter(r["categoria"] for r in rs).most_common(2)),
                  ", ".join(f"{k or 'vacío'} ({v})" for k, v in
                            Counter(r["idioma_declarado"]
                                    for r in rs).most_common(2)),
                  f"{sum(1 for r in rs if r['n_doblajes_auto']) / n * 100:.0f} %",
                  fmt(float(med([r["n_doblajes_auto"] for r in rs])), 0),
                  f"{fij['si']} sí, {fij['no']} no, "
                  f"{fij['sin_comentarios']} sin comentarios"))
    tabla("Descripción, etiquetas, categoría, idioma, doblaje y comentario "
          "fijado por canal",
          ["Canal", "n", "Mediana de caracteres de la descripción",
           "Con texto además de hashtags", "Mediana de etiquetas ocultas",
           "Categoría (veces)", "Idioma declarado (veces)",
           "Con doblaje automático", "Mediana de idiomas doblados",
           "Comentario fijado"], t)
    tabla("Doblaje automático frente al índice (todos)", CAB_IND,
          grupo_indice(filas, lambda r: "con doblaje automático"
                       if r["n_doblajes_auto"] else "sin doblaje"))
    tabla("Comentario fijado frente al índice (todos)", CAB_IND,
          grupo_indice(filas, lambda r: {"si": "con comentario fijado",
                                         "no": "sin comentario fijado"}
                       .get(r["comentario_fijado"])))
    idi = Counter()
    for r in filas:
        idi.update(x for x in r["idiomas_audio"].split("|") if x)
    print("\nIdiomas de audio más frecuentes:",
          ", ".join(f"{k} ({v})" for k, v in idi.most_common(14)))
    fijados = [r for r in filas if r["comentario_fijado"] == "si"]
    print(f"\nEjemplos de comentarios fijados ({len(fijados)} en total):")
    vistos = Counter()
    for r in fijados:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Mide los metadatos publicos de los Shorts recientes de los canales lideres.

Uso:
    python investigacion/medir_competencia.py recoger [--por-canal 40]
    python investigacion/medir_competencia.py analizar

"recoger" lee la pestana de Shorts de cada canal con yt-dlp (sin descargar
video), pide los metadatos completos de los N mas recientes y escribe
investigacion/metadatos-competencia.csv. "analizar" lee ese CSV e imprime las
tablas que se citan en docs/08-descubrimiento-y-metadatos.md.

Requisitos: yt-dlp en el PATH, Node (yt-dlp lo usa con --js-runtimes node) y
Python 3.10 o superior. No usa ninguna clave ni cuenta: solo datos publicos.
Las respuestas por video se guardan en una carpeta temporal para poder
reanudar sin repetir peticiones.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import re
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path

AQUI = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
CSV_SALIDA = AQUI / "metadatos-competencia.csv"
CACHE = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "medir_competencia_cache"

# (nombre, id del canal, idioma del canal, grupo)
CANALES = [
    ("studby", "UCHQ6IK7bgQM_BkAYqOy7nXA", "en", "lider"),
    ("GreenBroRants", "UCMA3DbSKleVofUC_5KetUMg", "en", "lider"),
    ("VoidCast", "UCyyGQfCJdADdby5IVe0-EGw", "en", "lider"),
    ("Gelo Stories", "UCUayw3SkGYlGK_XosKVbtZg", "en", "lider"),
    ("R6Rants", "UCdhQwHEYe8kKJn4Zv5dyPiA", "en", "mediano"),
    ("FriendBob", "UCbzGSJcaYRHAFlRQDTZU9OA", "en", "tardio"),
    ("SoyGelo", "UChEkE9e8zXMgmNNoTUTiHJg", "es", "lider"),
    ("Custerk Blox", "UCcN2eyGprJfFdIhsY7Jng4Q", "es", "lider"),
    ("Xenost", "UC6VBobwMlMuAQPcc04ImdLQ", "en", "vecino"),
]

COLUMNAS = [
    "canal", "canal_id", "idioma_canal", "grupo", "posicion", "video_id",
    "url", "titulo", "duracion_s", "vistas", "me_gusta", "publicado_utc",
    "dia_semana_utc", "hora_utc", "descripcion", "hashtags_descripcion",
    "hashtags_titulo", "n_hashtags", "etiquetas", "n_etiquetas", "categoria",
    "idioma_declarado", "idiomas_audio", "n_doblajes_auto",
    "subtitulos_manuales", "comentario_fijado", "comentario_fijado_del_canal",
    "comentario_fijado_texto", "suscriptores", "capturado_utc",
]

DIAS = ["lunes", "martes", "miercoles", "jueves", "viernes", "sabado",
        "domingo"]
RE_HASHTAG = re.compile(r"#[\wÀ-ɏ]+", re.UNICODE)
PAUSA = 1.5  # segundos entre peticiones de cada hilo
HILOS = 3


def correr(args: list[str], intentos: int = 4) -> str:
    """Ejecuta yt-dlp con reintentos y espera creciente (por si hay 429)."""
    espera = 20
    for intento in range(1, intentos + 1):
        res = subprocess.run(
            ["yt-dlp", "--no-warnings", *args],
            capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace",
        )
        if res.returncode == 0 and res.stdout.strip():
            return res.stdout
        err = (res.stderr or "").strip().splitlines()[-1:] or ["sin salida"]
        print(f"  intento {intento} fallo: {err[0][:160]}", file=sys.stderr)
        if intento < intentos:
            time.sleep(espera)
            espera *= 2
    return ""


def listar_shorts(canal_id: str, n: int) -> list[str]:
    salida = correr([
        "--flat-playlist", "--playlist-end", str(n), "--print", "id",
        f"https://www.youtube.com/channel/{canal_id}/shorts",
    ])
    return [x.strip() for x in salida.splitlines() if x.strip()]


def metadatos(video_id: str) -> dict | None:
    """Metadatos completos de un video, con cache en disco."""
    CACHE.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    archivo = CACHE / f"{video_id}.json"
    if archivo.exists():
        return json.loads(archivo.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    salida = correr([
        "--js-runtimes", "node", "--skip-download", "--dump-json",
        "--write-comments",
        "--extractor-args",
        "youtube:max_comments=1,1,0,0;comment_sort=top",
        f"https://www.youtube.com/shorts/{video_id}",
    ])
    time.sleep(PAUSA)
    if not salida:
        return None
    d = json.loads(salida)
    audio = {}
    for f in d.get("formats") or []:
        if f.get("vcodec") == "none" and f.get("acodec") not in (None, "none"):
            idioma = f.get("language")
            if idioma:
                nota = (f.get("format_note") or "").lower()
                audio.setdefault(idioma, False)
                if "dubbed-auto" in nota:
                    audio[idioma] = True
    com = (d.get("comments") or [None])[0]
    slim = {
        "id": d.get("id"),
        "title": d.get("title"),
        "duration": d.get("duration"),
        "view_count": d.get("view_count"),
        "like_count": d.get("like_count"),
        "timestamp": d.get("timestamp"),
        "description": d.get("description") or "",
        "tags": d.get("tags") or [],
        "categories": d.get("categories") or [],
        "language": d.get("language"),
        "audio": audio,
        "subtitles": sorted((d.get("subtitles") or {}).keys()),
        "comments_fetched": d.get("comments") is not None,
        "first_comment": None if not com else {
            "is_pinned": bool(com.get("is_pinned")),
            "author_is_uploader": bool(com.get("author_is_uploader")),
            "text": com.get("text") or "",
        },
        "channel_follower_count": d.get("channel_follower_count"),
        "captured": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
    }
    archivo.write_text(json.dumps(slim, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    return slim


def fila(canal, pos: int, d: dict) -> dict:
    nombre, canal_id, idioma, grupo = canal
    ts = d.get("timestamp")
    pub = datetime.fromtimestamp(ts, timezone.utc) if ts else None
    desc = d["description"]
    h_desc = RE_HASHTAG.findall(desc)
    h_tit = RE_HASHTAG.findall(d.get("title") or "")
    com = d.get("first_comment")
    if not d.get("comments_fetched") or com is None:
        fijado = "sin_comentarios"
    else:
        fijado = "si" if com["is_pinned"] else "no"
    es_fijado = fijado == "si"
    return {
        "canal": nombre, "canal_id": canal_id, "idioma_canal": idioma,
        "grupo": grupo, "posicion": pos, "video_id": d["id"],
        "url": f"https://www.youtube.com/shorts/{d['id']}",
        "titulo": d.get("title") or "",
        "duracion_s": d.get("duration"),
        "vistas": d.get("view_count"),
        "me_gusta": d.get("like_count"),
        "publicado_utc": pub.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ") if pub else "",
        "dia_semana_utc": DIAS[pub.weekday()] if pub else "",
        "hora_utc": pub.hour if pub else "",
        "descripcion": desc,
        "hashtags_descripcion": " ".join(h_desc),
        "hashtags_titulo": " ".join(h_tit),
        "n_hashtags": len(h_desc) + len(h_tit),
        "etiquetas": "|".join(d["tags"]),
        "n_etiquetas": len(d["tags"]),
        "categoria": "|".join(d["categories"]),
        "idioma_declarado": d.get("language") or "",
        "idiomas_audio": "|".join(sorted(d["audio"])),
        "n_doblajes_auto": sum(1 for v in d["audio"].values() if v),
        "subtitulos_manuales": "|".join(d["subtitles"]),
        "comentario_fijado": fijado,
        "comentario_fijado_del_canal":
            ("si" if com["author_is_uploader"] else "no") if es_fijado else "",
        "comentario_fijado_texto": com["text"] if es_fijado else "",
        "suscriptores": d.get("channel_follower_count"),
        "capturado_utc": d.get("captured"),
    }


def recoger(por_canal: int) -> None:
    filas = []
    for canal in CANALES:
        ids = listar_shorts(canal[1], por_canal)
        print(f"{canal[0]}: {len(ids)} shorts en la lista", flush=True)
        time.sleep(PAUSA)
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=HILOS) as pool:
            datos = list(pool.map(metadatos, ids))
        ok = 0
        for pos, d in enumerate(datos, start=1):
            if d:
                filas.append(fila(canal, pos, d))
                ok += 1
        print(f"  {ok} con metadatos completos", flush=True)
        escribir(filas)
    print(f"Listo: {len(filas)} filas en {CSV_SALIDA}")


def escribir(filas: list[dict]) -> None:
    with CSV_SALIDA.open("w", encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=COLUMNAS, quoting=csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL)
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(filas)


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="orden", required=True)
    r = sub.add_parser("recoger")
    r.add_argument("--por-canal", type=int, default=40)
    sub.add_parser("analizar")
    a = p.parse_args()
    if hasattr(sys.stdout, "reconfigure"):
        sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
    if a.orden == "recoger":
        recoger(a.por_canal)
    else:
        analizar()


def analizar() -> None:
    raise SystemExit("pendiente")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

RE_EMOJI = re.compile(
    "[\U0001F000-\U0001FAFF\u2600-\u27BF\u2B00-\u2BFF\uFE0F\u200D]")
RE_PALABRA = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z\u00C0-\u024F0-9']+")


def med(xs):
    xs = [x for x in xs if x is not None]
    return statistics.median(xs) if xs else None


def fmt(x, dec=2):
    if x is None:
        return "s/d"
    if isinstance(x, float) and dec == 0:
        return f"{x:,.0f}".replace(",", ".")
    if isinstance(x, float):
        return f"{x:.{dec}f}".replace(".", ",")
    return f"{x:,}".replace(",", ".")


def tabla(titulo, cabecera, filas):
    print(f"\n### {titulo}\n")
    print("| " + " | ".join(cabecera) + " |")
    print("|" + "---|" * len(cabecera))
    for f in filas:
        print("| " + " | ".join(str(c) for c in f) + " |")


def marca(n):
    return f"{n}" if n >= N_MINIMO else f"{n} (muestra chica)"


def spearman(xs, ys):
    def rangos(v):
        orden = sorted(range(len(v)), key=lambda i: v[i])
        r = [0.0] * len(v)
        i = 0
        while i < len(orden):
            j = i
            while j + 1 < len(orden) and v[orden[j + 1]] == v[orden[i]]:
                j += 1
            for k in range(i, j + 1):
                r[orden[k]] = (i + j) / 2 + 1
            i = j + 1
        return r
    if len(xs) < 5:
        return None
    rx, ry = rangos(xs), rangos(ys)
    mx, my = statistics.mean(rx), statistics.mean(ry)
    num = sum((a - mx) * (b - my) for a, b in zip(rx, ry))
    den = (sum((a - mx) ** 2 for a in rx) * sum((b - my) ** 2 for b in ry))
    return num / den ** 0.5 if den else None


def limpiar_titulo(t):
    """Titulo sin hashtags ni emojis, para contar palabras."""
    t = RE_HASHTAG.sub("", t)
    t = RE_EMOJI.sub("", t)
    return " ".join(t.split())


def cargar():
    with CSV_SALIDA.open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
        filas = list(csv.DictReader(f))
    for r in filas:
        for k in ("duracion_s", "vistas", "me_gusta", "n_hashtags",
                  "n_etiquetas", "n_doblajes_auto", "posicion"):
            r[k] = int(r[k]) if r[k] not in ("", None) else None
        r["pub"] = datetime.strptime(
            r["publicado_utc"], "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"
        ).replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
        cap = datetime.fromisoformat(r["capturado_utc"])
        r["edad_h"] = (cap - r["pub"]).total_seconds() / 3600
        r["maduro"] = r["edad_h"] >= EDAD_MINIMA_H
        limpio = limpiar_titulo(r["titulo"])
        r["titulo_limpio"] = limpio
        palabras = RE_PALABRA.findall(limpio)
        r["palabras"] = palabras
        r["n_palabras"] = len(palabras)
        r["n_car"] = len(r["titulo"])
        mayus = [p for p in palabras
                 if len(p) >= 2 and p.isupper() and any(c.isalpha() for c in p)]
        r["n_mayus"] = len(mayus)
        letras = [c for c in limpio if c.isalpha()]
        r["todo_mayus"] = bool(letras) and all(c.isupper() for c in letras)
        r["emoji"] = bool(RE_EMOJI.search(r["titulo"]))
        r["pub_col"] = r["pub"] - timedelta(hours=5)
    # indice relativo: vistas / mediana del propio canal (solo maduros)
    por_canal = defaultdict(list)
    for r in filas:
        por_canal[r["canal"]].append(r)
    for canal, rs in por_canal.items():
        m = med([r["vistas"] for r in rs if r["maduro"]])
        for r in rs:
            r["indice"] = (r["vistas"] / m) if (m and r["maduro"]) else None
    return filas, por_canal


def grupo_indice(filas, clave, orden=None):
    """Mediana del indice relativo por grupo. Devuelve filas de tabla."""
    g = defaultdict(list)
    for r in filas:
        if r["indice"] is not None:
            k = clave(r)
            if k is not None:
                g[k].append(r["indice"])
    llaves = orden if orden else sorted(g)
    out = []
    for k in llaves:
        v = g.get(k, [])
        if not v:
            continue
        sobre = sum(1 for x in v if x >= 2) / len(v) * 100
        out.append((k, marca(len(v)), fmt(med(v)), f"{sobre:.0f} %"))
    return out


CAB_IND = ["Grupo", "n", "Mediana del índice", "Con índice de 2 o más"]


def tramo_palabras(r):
    n = r["n_palabras"]
    if n <= 2:
        return "1 a 2 palabras"
    if n <= 4:
        return "3 a 4 palabras"
    if n <= 7:
        return "5 a 7 palabras"
    if n <= 10:
        return "8 a 10 palabras"
    return "11 o más palabras"


ORD_PAL = ["1 a 2 palabras", "3 a 4 palabras", "5 a 7 palabras",
           "8 a 10 palabras", "11 o más palabras"]


def tramo_dur(r):
    d = r["duracion_s"]
    if d is None:
        return None
    for tope, nombre in ((60, "hasta 59 s"), (90, "60 a 89 s"),
                         (120, "90 a 119 s"), (150, "120 a 149 s")):
        if d < tope:
            return nombre
    return "150 a 185 s"


ORD_DUR = ["hasta 59 s", "60 a 89 s", "90 a 119 s", "120 a 149 s",
           "150 a 185 s"]


def franja(h):
    ini = h // 3 * 3
    return f"{ini:02d} a {ini + 2:02d} h"


def analizar() -> None:
    filas, por_canal = cargar()
    nombres = [c[0] for c in CANALES if c[0] in por_canal]
    en = [r for r in filas if r["idioma_canal"] == "en"]
    es = [r for r in filas if r["idioma_canal"] == "es"]
    formato_en = [r for r in en if r["grupo"] != "vecino"]
    maduros = [r for r in filas if r["maduro"]]
    print(f"Filas: {len(filas)}; maduras (>= {EDAD_MINIMA_H} h): "
          f"{len(maduros)}; en inglés: {len(en)}; en español: {len(es)}")
    print("Índice = vistas del video / mediana de vistas de los videos "
          "maduros del mismo canal.")

    # 1. Resumen por canal
    t = []
    for c in nombres:
        rs = por_canal[c]
        mad = [r for r in rs if r["maduro"]]
        fechas = sorted(r["pub"] for r in rs)
        dias = max((fechas[-1] - fechas[0]).total_seconds() / 86400, 0.01)
        t.append((c, len(rs), len(mad),
                  fechas[0].strftime("%m-%d") + " a "
                  + fechas[-1].strftime("%m-%d"),
                  fmt(float(med([r["vistas"] for r in mad]) or 0), 0),
                  fmt(float(med([r["duracion_s"] for r in rs])), 0),
                  fmt((len(rs) - 1) / dias, 1)))
    tabla("Resumen por canal",
          ["Canal", "n", "n maduros", "Rango de fechas (UTC)",
           "Mediana de vistas (maduros)", "Mediana de duración (s)",
           "Videos por día"], t)

    # 2. Forma del titulo por canal
    t = []
    for c in nombres:
        rs = por_canal[c]
        n = len(rs)
        t.append((c, n,
                  fmt(float(med([r["n_palabras"] for r in rs])), 0),
                  fmt(float(med([r["n_car"] for r in rs])), 0),
                  f"{sum(1 for r in rs if r['n_mayus']) / n * 100:.0f} %",
                  f"{sum(1 for r in rs if r['todo_mayus']) / n * 100:.0f} %",
                  f"{sum(1 for r in rs if r['emoji']) / n * 100:.0f} %",
                  f"{sum(1 for r in rs if r['hashtags_titulo']) / n * 100:.0f} %"))
    tabla("Forma del título por canal",
          ["Canal", "n", "Mediana de palabras", "Mediana de caracteres",
           "Con palabra en MAYÚSCULAS", "Todo en mayúsculas", "Con emoji",
           "Con hashtag en el título"], t)

    # 3. Longitud del titulo frente al indice
    tabla("Palabras del título frente al índice (canales en inglés del "
          "formato)", CAB_IND, grupo_indice(formato_en, tramo_palabras, ORD_PAL))
    tabla("Palabras del título frente al índice (canales en español)",
          CAB_IND, grupo_indice(es, tramo_palabras, ORD_PAL))
    t = []
    for c in nombres:
        mad = [r for r in por_canal[c] if r["maduro"]]
        if len(mad) < 8:
            continue
        orden = sorted(mad, key=lambda r: -r["vistas"])
        k = max(len(orden) // 4, 1)
        top, resto = orden[:k], orden[k:]
        rho = spearman([r["n_palabras"] for r in mad],
                       [r["vistas"] for r in mad])
        t.append((c, len(mad), k,
                  fmt(float(med([r["n_palabras"] for r in top])), 1),
                  fmt(float(med([r["n_palabras"] for r in resto])), 1),
                  fmt(float(med([r["n_car"] for r in top])), 0),
                  fmt(float(med([r["n_car"] for r in resto])), 0),
                  fmt(rho)))
    tabla("Cuartil superior de vistas frente al resto, por canal",
          ["Canal", "n maduros", "n cuartil superior",
           "Palabras (cuartil superior)", "Palabras (resto)",
           "Caracteres (cuartil superior)", "Caracteres (resto)",
           "Spearman palabras y vistas"], t)

    # 4. Mayusculas y emoji
    def caps(r):
        if r["todo_mayus"]:
            return "todo en mayúsculas"
        return "con palabra en MAYÚSCULAS" if r["n_mayus"] else "sin mayúsculas"
    tabla("Mayúsculas frente al índice (inglés, formato)", CAB_IND,
          grupo_indice(formato_en, caps))
    tabla("Mayúsculas frente al índice (español)", CAB_IND,
          grupo_indice(es, caps))
    tabla("Emoji en el título frente al índice (todos)", CAB_IND,
          grupo_indice(filas, lambda r: "con emoji" if r["emoji"]
                       else "sin emoji"))

    # 5. Palabras iniciales
    for nombre, sub in (("inglés, formato", formato_en), ("español", es),
                        ("Xenost, vecino", por_canal.get("Xenost", []))):
        c1 = Counter()
        ind = defaultdict(list)
        for r in sub:
            if not r["palabras"]:
                continue
            for k in (1, 2):
                ini = " ".join(p.lower() for p in r["palabras"][:k])
                c1[(k, ini)] += 1
                if r["indice"] is not None:
                    ind[(k, ini)].append(r["indice"])
        t = [(f"{ini}", k, n, marca(len(ind[(k, ini)])),
              fmt(med(ind[(k, ini)])))
             for (k, ini), n in c1.most_common(40) if n >= 4]
        tabla(f"Arranques de título más frecuentes ({nombre}, "
              f"n total {len(sub)})",
              ["Arranque", "Palabras", "Veces", "n maduros",
               "Mediana del índice"], t[:16])

    # 6. Hashtags
    t = []
    for c in nombres:
        rs = por_canal[c]
        cnt = Counter()
        for r in rs:
            cnt.update(h.lower() for h in
                       (r["hashtags_descripcion"] + " "
                        + r["hashtags_titulo"]).split())
        t.append((c, len(rs),
                  fmt(float(med([r["n_hashtags"] for r in rs])), 0),
                  f"{min(r['n_hashtags'] for r in rs)} a "
                  f"{max(r['n_hashtags'] for r in rs)}",
                  f"{sum(1 for r in rs if '#shorts' in (r['hashtags_descripcion'] + ' ' + r['hashtags_titulo']).lower().split()) / len(rs) * 100:.0f} %",
                  ", ".join(f"{h} ({n})" for h, n in cnt.most_common(6))))
    tabla("Hashtags por canal",
          ["Canal", "n", "Mediana de hashtags", "Rango", "Usa #shorts",
           "Más usados (veces)"], t)
    tabla("Número de hashtags frente al índice (todos)", CAB_IND,
          grupo_indice(filas, lambda r: "0" if r["n_hashtags"] == 0 else
                       "1 a 3" if r["n_hashtags"] <= 3 else
                       "4 a 5" if r["n_hashtags"] <= 5 else "6 o más",
                       ["0", "1 a 3", "4 a 5", "6 o más"]))

    # 7. Descripcion, etiquetas, categoria, idioma, doblaje, fijado
    t = []
    for c in nombres:
        rs = por_canal[c]
        n = len(rs)
        sin_h = [len(RE_HASHTAG.sub("", r["descripcion"]).strip()) for r in rs]
        fij = Counter(r["comentario_fijado"] for r in rs)
        t.append((c, n,
                  fmt(float(med([len(r["descripcion"]) for r in rs])), 0),
                  f"{sum(1 for x in sin_h if x > 0) / n * 100:.0f} %",
                  fmt(float(med([r["n_etiquetas"] for r in rs])), 0),
                  ", ".join(f"{k} ({v})" for k, v in
                            Counter(r["categoria"] for r in rs).most_common(2)),
                  ", ".join(f"{k or 'vacío'} ({v})" for k, v in
                            Counter(r["idioma_declarado"]
                                    for r in rs).most_common(2)),
                  f"{sum(1 for r in rs if r['n_doblajes_auto']) / n * 100:.0f} %",
                  fmt(float(med([r["n_doblajes_auto"] for r in rs])), 0),
                  f"{fij['si']} sí, {fij['no']} no, "
                  f"{fij['sin_comentarios']} sin comentarios"))
    tabla("Descripción, etiquetas, categoría, idioma, doblaje y comentario "
          "fijado por canal",
          ["Canal", "n", "Mediana de caracteres de la descripción",
           "Con texto además de hashtags", "Mediana de etiquetas ocultas",
           "Categoría (veces)", "Idioma declarado (veces)",
           "Con doblaje automático", "Mediana de idiomas doblados",
           "Comentario fijado"], t)
    tabla("Doblaje automático frente al índice (todos)", CAB_IND,
          grupo_indice(filas, lambda r: "con doblaje automático"
                       if r["n_doblajes_auto"] else "sin doblaje"))
    tabla("Comentario fijado frente al índice (todos)", CAB_IND,
          grupo_indice(filas, lambda r: {"si": "con comentario fijado",
                                         "no": "sin comentario fijado"}
                       .get(r["comentario_fijado"])))
    idi = Counter()
    for r in filas:
        idi.update(x for x in r["idiomas_audio"].split("|") if x)
    print("\nIdiomas de audio más frecuentes:",
          ", ".join(f"{k} ({v})" for k, v in idi.most_common(14)))
    fijados = [r for r in filas if r["comentario_fijado"] == "si"]
    print(f"\nEjemplos de comentarios fijados ({len(fijados)} en total):")
    vistos = Counter()
    for r in fijados:
        if vistos[r["canal"]] < 4:
            vistos[r["canal"]] += 1
            txt = " ".join(r["comentario_fijado_texto"].split())[:150]
            print(f"- {r['canal']} (del canal: "
                  f"{r['comentario_fijado_del_canal']}): {txt}")

    # 8. Duracion
    tabla("Duración frente al índice (inglés, formato)", CAB_IND,
          grupo_indice(formato_en, tramo_dur, ORD_DUR))
    tabla("Duración frente al índice (español)", CAB_IND,
          grupo_indice(es, tramo_dur, ORD_DUR))
    t = []
    for c in nombres:
        rs = por_canal[c]
        mad = [r for r in rs if r["maduro"]]
        d = sorted(r["duracion_s"] for r in rs)
        t.append((c, len(rs), d[0], fmt(float(med(d)), 0), d[-1],
                  f"{sum(1 for x in d if x > 60) / len(d) * 100:.0f} %",
                  len(mad),
                  fmt(spearman([r["duracion_s"] for r in mad],
                               [r["vistas"] for r in mad]))))
    tabla("Duración por canal",
          ["Canal", "n", "Mínima (s)", "Mediana (s)", "Máxima (s)",
           "De más de 60 s", "n maduros", "Spearman duración y vistas"], t)

    # 9. Dia y hora
    for nombre, sub in (("inglés, formato", formato_en), ("español", es)):
        cnt = Counter(r["pub"].weekday() for r in sub)
        ind = defaultdict(list)
        for r in sub:
            if r["indice"] is not None:
                ind[r["pub"].weekday()].append(r["indice"])
        tabla(f"Día de publicación en UTC ({nombre})",
              ["Día", "Publicados", "n maduros", "Mediana del índice"],
              [(DIAS[d], cnt[d], marca(len(ind[d])), fmt(med(ind[d])))
               for d in range(7) if cnt[d]])
        cnt = Counter(franja(r["pub"].hour) for r in sub)
        ind = defaultdict(list)
        for r in sub:
            if r["indice"] is not None:
                ind[franja(r["pub"].hour)].append(r["indice"])
        t = []
        for h in range(0, 24, 3):
            k = franja(h)
            if cnt[k]:
                col = (h - 5) % 24
                t.append((k, f"{col:02d} a {(col + 2) % 24:02d} h", cnt[k],
                          f"{cnt[k] / len(sub) * 100:.0f} %",
                          marca(len(ind[k])), fmt(med(ind[k]))))
        tabla(f"Franja horaria de publicación ({nombre})",
              ["Franja UTC", "Hora de Colombia", "Publicados",
               "Parte del total", "n maduros", "Mediana del índice"], t)
    t = []
    for c in nombres:
        rs = por_canal[c]
        horas = Counter(r["pub"].hour for r in rs)
        top = horas.most_common(4)
        minutos = Counter(r["pub"].minute for r in rs)
        en_punto = sum(v for m, v in minutos.items() if m % 15 == 0)
        t.append((c, len(rs),
                  ", ".join(f"{h:02d} h ({n})" for h, n in top),
                  len(horas),
                  f"{en_punto / len(rs) * 100:.0f} %"))
    tabla("Horas UTC preferidas por canal",
          ["Canal", "n", "Horas más usadas (veces)", "Horas distintas usadas",
           "Publicados en minuto 00, 15, 30 o 45"], t)

    # 10. Cadencia
    t = []
    for c in nombres:
        rs = sorted(por_canal[c], key=lambda r: r["pub"])
        huecos = [(b["pub"] - a["pub"]).total_seconds() / 3600
                  for a, b in zip(rs, rs[1:])]
        por_dia = Counter(r["pub"].date() for r in rs)
        # dias completos: se descartan el primero y el ultimo del rango
        dias = sorted(por_dia)
        completos = [por_dia[d] for d in dias[1:-1]] or list(por_dia.values())
        t.append((c, len(rs), fmt(float(med(huecos)), 1),
                  fmt(float(min(huecos)), 1), fmt(float(max(huecos)), 1),
                  fmt(float(med(completos)), 1), max(por_dia.values()),
                  len(dias)))
    tabla("Cadencia por canal",
          ["Canal", "n", "Mediana de horas entre videos", "Mínimo (h)",
           "Máximo (h)", "Mediana de videos por día completo",
           "Máximo en un día", "Días con publicación"], t)

    # 11. Los mejores y peores titulos
    for nombre, sub in (("inglés, formato", formato_en), ("español", es)):
        mad = sorted([r for r in sub if r["indice"] is not None],
                     key=lambda r: -r["indice"])
        tabla(f"Los 12 títulos con mayor índice ({nombre})",
              ["Índice", "Canal", "Vistas", "Duración (s)", "Título"],
              [(fmt(r["indice"]), r["canal"], fmt(r["vistas"]),
                r["duracion_s"], r["titulo"]) for r in mad[:12]])
        tabla(f"Los 8 títulos con menor índice ({nombre})",
              ["Índice", "Canal", "Vistas", "Duración (s)", "Título"],
              [(fmt(r["indice"]), r["canal"], fmt(r["vistas"]),
                r["duracion_s"], r["titulo"]) for r in mad[-8:]])

    # 12. Me gusta
    t = []
    for c in nombres:
        mad = [r for r in por_canal[c] if r["maduro"] and r["me_gusta"]
               and r["vistas"]]
        if not mad:
            continue
        tasas = [r["me_gusta"] / r["vistas"] * 100 for r in mad]
        t.append((c, len(mad), fmt(med(tasas)),
                  fmt(spearman(tasas, [r["vistas"] for r in mad]))))
    tabla("Me gusta por cada 100 vistas (videos maduros)",
          ["Canal", "n", "Mediana (%)", "Spearman tasa y vistas"], t)

The `support.google.com/youtube/blog/...` and `/thread/...` community posts returned only navigation, so their contents are cited through press coverage.

## 1. Ranking signals

- [OFFICIAL] General recommendation inputs: "viewing behaviour, likes, dislikes, subscriptions and feedback, including from satisfaction surveys" (How YouTube Works, undated) https://www.youtube.com/howyoutubeworks/product-features/recommendations/

Thresholds are not published. https://www.searchenginejournal.com/youtube-explains-how-shorts-algorithm-works/494953/ (video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n3jsYK_-aRU)
- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] Todd Beaupré, Creator Insider, 1 Sep 2026: "We have to look at many different metrics, because no metric on its own is a good indicator of value."; "our North Star is: long-term user value." https://outlierkit.com/resources/how-youtube-recommendations-work/ (video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rHLjxrbXmmY)
- [OFFICIAL] Since 25 Jun 2026 Shorts have no dislike button and a heart replaces the thumbs-up: "we're also retiring the dislike button", in order "to more accurately tune your feed". (The YouTube Team) https://blog.youtube/news-and-events/youtube-shorts-experience-updates-features/
- [THIRD-PARTY] "Not interested" now asks for a reason; "Don't recommend this channel" remains. (ppc.land, 25 Jun 2026) https://ppc.land/youtube-shorts-removes-dislike-button-adds-heart-icon-and-2x-speed/
- [UNVERIFIED] Any official weighting of viewed vs swiped away, replays/loops, shares, comments or subscriptions from a Short. No official statement found that the "viewed vs swiped away" analytics figure is itself the ranking signal.
- [THIRD-PARTY] Social Media Today's summary lists watch time, re-watches, likes, shares and comments (its own list, not a staff quote). https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/youtube-advice-for-shorts-creators-hashtags-algorithm/691835/
- [UNVERIFIED] Paddy Galloway's "70 to 90% viewed" range appeared only in search snippets.

## 2. View counting, engaged views, YPP

- [OFFICIAL] "Starting 3/31/2025, we're updating how Shorts views are counted." "Views will count the number of times a Short starts to play or replay, with no minimum watch time requirement." The old metric is kept as "Engaged views". https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/10059070?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL] Same page: "This change will not directly impact the YouTube Partner Program (YPP) eligibility and Shorts ad revenue sharing." "They will both be based on 'Engaged Shorts views.'"
- [OFFICIAL] "For the purposes of calculating payments, YouTube uses eligible 'Engaged views'." https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/12504220?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL] Current YPP entry: "Get 1,000 subscribers with 4,000 qualified watch hours in the last 12 months" or "1,000 subscribers with 10 million qualified Shorts views in the last 90 days." https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/72851?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL] From 1 Feb 2027, new applicants need "8,000 qualified watch hours in the last 365 days" "or 20 million qualified Shorts views in the last 90 days". (The YouTube Team, 10 Aug 2026) https://blog.youtube/news-and-events/youtube-partner-program-updates-2027-new-opportunities-earn/
- [OFFICIAL] Same post: from 1 Feb 2027, Shorts revenue sharing only for "creators who have 10 million qualified Shorts views over the last 90 days"; "Channels below this threshold remain in YPP and continue earning on long-form content".
- [THIRD-PARTY] Fan funding/Shopping tier unchanged at 500 subscribers, 3 uploads in 90 days, and 3,000 watch hours or 3M Shorts views. (SEJ, 11 Aug 2026) https://www.searchenginejournal.com/youtube-updates-partner-program-terms-shorts-payout-rules/585331/ Not found on the official pages I opened.
- [THIRD-PARTY] From 24 Aug 2026 long-form public views also count from first frame; earnings stay on engaged metrics. (Engadget, 17 Aug 2026) https://engadget.com/2238611/youtube-public-view-counts-will-likely-get-higher-starting-next-week/ Official post not opened: https://support.google.com/youtube/thread/433409976?hl=en

## 3. Seed audience, long tail, freshness

- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] Sherman, Aug 2023: the algorithms "effectively find like a seed audience, find a set of people that may enjoy your video." A Short can rise then stall depending on that audience's response. (TechCrunch, 25 Aug 2023) https://techcrunch.com/2023/08/25/youtube-demystifies-the-shorts-algorithm-views-and-answers-other-creator-questions/
- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] Beaupré, 1 Sep 2026, on a first video: "we hope that we'll find some viewers who are interested, and build from there"; "if we don't, then maybe that video just won't get more impressions." https://outlierkit.com/resources/how-youtube-recommends-new-channels/
- [OFFICIAL] The only official recency statement found: "The Shorts feed, with its snackable and trendy nature, may tune up on the recency of content". (YouTube Help, undated) https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/16559651?hl=en
- [THIRD-PARTY] The "30 days" report comes from Mario Joos (retention strategist), not YouTube: from mid-September 2025, Shorts older than about 28 to 30 days lost impressions. He calls it "a carefully constructed working theory and not a confirmed fact." SEJ says YouTube has not confirmed any change. (5 Dec 2025) https://www.searchenginejournal.com/youtube-shorts-algorithm-may-now-favor-fresh-over-evergreen/562661/
- [THIRD-PARTY] Tubefilter asked Google for comment and reported none. (5 Dec 2025) https://www.tubefilter.com/2025/12/05/youtube-shorts-algorithm-change-new-uploads/
- [THIRD-PARTY, search snippet only] OverseerOS tracked 9,982 Shorts: 90.5% kept gaining views, mostly very few. https://www.overseeros.com/blog/do-youtube-shorts-get-views-after-30-days
- [OFFICIAL] The FAQ's "An old video recently took off, why?" answer is about videos in general (rising topic, new viewers bingeing), not Shorts. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/141805?hl=en
- [UNVERIFIED] No official statement that a Short is "pushed again" on a schedule, or that Shorts have a long tail.

## 4. Upload frequency, several Shorts a day

- [OFFICIAL] "growth in views across uploads is not correlated with time between uploads." Taking a break does not hurt either. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/141805?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] Sherman, Aug 2023: "There is nothing in our systems that's like when you hit the five video or 10 short threshold per day" (auto-transcript quote via https://outlierkit.com/resources/youtube-shorts-algorithm/); "that energy is probably better spent in just making a better video and fewer of them." (Social Media Today, 24 Aug 2023) https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/youtube-advice-for-shorts-creators-hashtags-algorithm/691835/
- [OFFICIAL] There is a technical daily upload cap with no published number: standard access has a "limited daily limit", higher tiers a "higher daily limit". https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/9890437?hl=en
- [UNVERIFIED] No official statement on Shorts cannibalising each other.
- [THIRD-PARTY, search snippet only] OverseerOS (18,148 Shorts): gaps of 12 to 48 hours often beat gaps under 3 hours; correlational. https://www.overseeros.com/blog/how-long-to-wait-between-youtube-shorts

## 5. Time of day

- [OFFICIAL] "Publish time is not known to impact a video's long-term performance." Posting when the audience is active may help early views. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/141805?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] Sherman, Aug 2023: "It's not something that we think about optimizing for." (via outlierkit, link above; TechCrunch notes news content as the exception.)
- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] Rene Ritchie: "Waiting 24 to 48 hours is no different than waiting 24 to 48 seconds or weeks or months. All you're doing is waiting." (SEJ, 12 Nov 2025) https://www.searchenginejournal.com/youtube-debunks-24-48-hour-upload-delay-recommendation/560613/ (video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Zf7tOh6y39o)
- [OFFICIAL] "Shorts don't trigger notifications on upload". (Rene's Top Five, 28 Mar 2024) https://blog.youtube/culture-and-trends/renes-top-five-on-youtube-march-28-2024-edition/

## 6. Deleting, re-uploading, poor performers

- [OFFICIAL] Beaupré, quoted on YouTube's blog: "Don't delete videos unless you have a very, very good reason." "When you delete a video, you delete your channel's connection to the audience that watched that video." (28 Mar 2024) https://blog.youtube/culture-and-trends/renes-top-five-on-youtube-march-28-2024-edition/
- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] Sherman on delete-and-repost: "I would not advise that." "there's also a risk that it gets seen as spam in our systems." (Social Media Today, 24 Aug 2023, link above)
- [OFFICIAL] An underperforming video does not hurt the channel by itself: "What matters is how viewers reply to each video when it's recommended to them." https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/141805?hl=en

## 7. Title, description, hashtags, category, language, tags

- [OFFICIAL] Tags: "Not important." (mainly for spelling variants). Changing title/thumbnail can help "but don't change what's working." https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/141805?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL] Hashtags: "Hashtags also allow viewers and listeners to find related content via search." "If a video or playlist has more than 60 hashtags, we'll ignore each hashtag". No mention of #shorts. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/6390658?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL] #shorts is not needed for classification: uploads from 15 Oct 2024 "with a square or vertical aspect ratio up to three minutes in length will be categorized as Shorts". https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/15424877?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] Sherman on hashtags: sometimes tied to events, "Other times they're focused on topics, and I think in both those cases, creators should consider using them." (Social Media Today, link above)
- [OFFICIAL] Video language setting: "It's also used to help viewers find videos in their language." https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/6304325?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] With no behavioural data, the system uses "the user's topical preferences and what we understand about what this video is about" (Beaupré, 1 Sep 2026, via outlierkit, link in topic 3).
- [UNVERIFIED] No official statement found on the category field affecting Shorts ranking.

## 8. Captions and dubbing

- [OFFICIAL] Automatic dubbing: "This feature is enabled by default for eligible creators." "When you upload a new video, dubs will be automatically generated." Not generated when there is little speech or the video exceeds 120 minutes. The page does not mention Shorts. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/15569972?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL] "Auto dubbing is available in 27 languages."; "having your videos dubbed has no negative impact on viewer discovery." (Rene Ritchie, 15 May 2026) https://blog.youtube/creator-and-artist-stories/youtube-auto-dubbing-explained/
- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] "all new content, both shorts and VODs, will be automatically dubbed upon upload" (Social Media Today, 24 Jun 2025) https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/youtube-expands-auto-dubbing-dream-screen-inspiration-tab/751554/
- [OFFICIAL] Manual multi-language audio covers Shorts ("to a single video or Short") but is "currently available to creators with access to Advanced features." Translated titles/descriptions are used by search. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13338784?hl=en
- [UNVERIFIED] Whether a brand-new, unverified channel gets auto-dubbing on Shorts; any official statement on captions affecting Shorts reach.

## 9. Playlists, series, related video

- [OFFICIAL] Shorts can be added to playlists from the Short's watch page; reordering "isn't available for playlists that only contain YouTube Shorts." https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/57792?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL] Made on YouTube 2026 recap (23 Sep 2026) mentions "structured Shorts series", with no details. https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/youtube/made-on-youtube-updates-2026/
- [THIRD-PARTY] Shorts series let creators "organize their Shorts into seasons and episodes", "rolling out starting today". (9to5Google, 23 Sep 2026) https://9to5google.com/2026/09/23/made-on-youtube-2026/ No official help page with steps found.

- [OFFICIAL] Pinned comments are listed under advanced features, which a new channel gets through channel history or ID/video verification. Tier placement is as read by the fetch tool; check the live table. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/9890437?hl=en

## 11. Shorts up to 3 minutes

- [OFFICIAL] Applies to uploads from "October 15, 2024", square or vertical, up to three minutes. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/15424877?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL] Shorts over one minute "with an active copyright claim of any type, including manual claims, will be blocked globally on YouTube." Blocked Shorts "will not be playable or recommended". Music: "You can use most songs for up to 90 seconds in a 3 minute Short." (same page)
- [OFFICIAL] "Shorts longer than one minute that have an active copyright claim, regardless of the policy, will be blocked on YouTube." https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/6013276?hl=en
- [UNVERIFIED] No official statement found that 1 to 3 minute Shorts are recommended differently from shorter ones. A vidIQ video reportedly claimed worse distribution (search snippet only).

## 12. Search

- [THIRD-PARTY] January 2026: a "Shorts" option was added to the search Type filter, and the duration bracket now starts at three minutes. (Tubefilter, 9 Jan 2026) https://www.tubefilter.com/2026/01/09/youtube-search-filters-shorts-vs-long-form/ Official post not readable: https://support.google.com/youtube/thread/400586735/changes-to-youtube-search-filters-to-improve-content-discovery
- [OFFICIAL] Hashtags and translated titles/descriptions feed search (topics 7 and 8).
- [UNVERIFIED] No official page found describing Shorts-specific search ranking.

## 13. Brand-new channel, Hype

- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] Beaupré, 1 Sep 2026: "When a new channel publishes for the first time, there are zero viewers who have that channel in their history." "Does that mean that they're not appealing to any viewer? No." https://outlierkit.com/resources/how-youtube-recommends-new-channels/
- [OFFICIAL] "For new channels, gaining this credibility and building a community takes time." https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/16559651?hl=en
- [UNVERIFIED] No official statement uses "warm-up" or "new channel penalty", confirming or denying.
- [OFFICIAL] Hype does not apply: "Channels in the YouTube Partner Program with 500 to 500,000 subscribers are eligible", and "YouTube Shorts" is on the not-eligible list. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/15509925?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL] Practical limits for a new channel: limited daily uploads at standard access; related video, pinned comments and multi-language audio need advanced access. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/9890437?hl=en

## 14. Thumbnails

- [OFFICIAL] Custom Shorts thumbnails exist since 24 Jul 2026: "YouTube Partner Program creators can start uploading custom thumbnails for Shorts." Also "three suggested thumbnail frames for Shorts on desktop"; "You can still pick any frame from the video through the YouTube app on mobile." https://blog.youtube/news-and-events/youtube-studio-custom-thumbnail-updates/
- [OFFICIAL] "Custom thumbnails for Shorts are currently only available to add in YouTube Studio on a computer."; account must be verified; 9:16 recommended. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/72431?hl=en
- The blog says YPP creators first, while the help page only mentions verification. For a non-YPP channel, assume frame selection only until you see the option.

## 15. Cross-posting

- [OFFICIAL] YouTube spam policy disallows "Re-posting material from other websites or platforms, or other videos without adding anything of your own". https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/2801973?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL] Views not counted for Shorts revenue include "Non-original Shorts" and reuploads of "other creators' content from YouTube or other platform". No mention of watermarks. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/12504220?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] 1 Oct 2026: "we're updating our recommendation systems to further prioritize original content" and "reduce the reach of content re-uploaded from other creators without adding anything of your own." (Social Media Today) https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/youtube-updates-shorts-algorithm-to-put-more-focus-on-original-content/831976/ Official post not readable: https://support.google.com/youtube/blog/470890423/prioritizing-original-content-on-shorts?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] Ritchie, same day: not enough are "VO descriptions of what's happening on screen, minor technical edits, or template-based bulk changes." (SEJ) https://www.searchenginejournal.com/youtube-original-shorts-reposted-clips-reach/591774/ (video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XS2A6aExLaA)
- [UNVERIFIED] No current official YouTube statement found on TikTok/Instagram watermarks, or on posting your own videos across platforms. The 2021 Shorts Fund watermark rule appeared only in press snippets.
- [OFFICIAL] Instagram (Mosseri, 31 May 2023): "We aim to make certain reels less visible for other reasons, such as low-resolution or watermarked reels". https://about.instagram.com/blog/announcements/instagram-ranking-explained
- [OFFICIAL] Instagram tips (31 May 2023; page served in Spanish): content with obvious watermarks, reposts of existing reels, and aggregator accounts are less likely to be recommended. https://creators.instagram.com/blog/tips-for-improving-your-reach
- [OFFICIAL] Instagram original content guidelines (undated, served in Spanish): accounts mostly posting unoriginal content may lose non-follower recommendations; eligibility returns when a significant share of posts over 30 days is original. https://creators.instagram.com/original-content-guidelines/
- [THIRD-PARTY, search snippet only] The April 2024 Instagram details (reposts replaced by originals; aggregators with 10+ reposts in 30 days removed from recommendations) come from Engadget. The official post SEJ cites was not opened: https://creators.instagram.com/blog/rewarding-original-creators-on-instagram
- [OFFICIAL] TikTok Community Guidelines (released 25 Aug 2026, effective 24 Sep 2026): "Content is also ineligible for the FYF if it includes unoriginal or reused material without anything new." https://www.tiktok.com/community-guidelines/en/integrity-authenticity
- [UNVERIFIED] TikTok watermark wording ("someone else's visible watermark or superimposed logo") appeared in a search snippet of https://www.tiktok.com/creator-academy/article/tiktok-originality-policy ; the page returned only navigation.

## 16. Inauthentic and reused content

- [OFFICIAL] 15 Jul 2025: "We are also renaming this policy from 'repetitious content' to 'inauthentic content.'"; it covers repetitive or mass-produced content. Reused content is repurposed content "without adding significant original commentary, substantive modifications, or educational or entertainment value." https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/1311392?hl=en

## 17. Altered/synthetic disclosure

- [OFFICIAL] "We require creators to disclose AI-generated or altered content that seems realistic." Not required for clearly unrealistic content, e.g. "Someone riding a unicorn through a fantastical world" and AI animation "in a fully animated video". https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/14328491?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL] Same page: AI help with script, outline, title or thumbnail needs no disclosure; "Disclosing AI content alone won't limit a video's audience or impact its eligibility to earn money."
- The page covers cloning your own voice (no disclosure) but does not explicitly address generic AI narration voices.

## 18. Made for kids

- [OFFICIAL] Unavailable on made-for-kids videos: comments, notification bell, personalised advertising, save to playlist/watch later, cards and end screens, miniplayer, among others. Shorts are not addressed separately. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/9527654?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL] Made-for-kids content is also excluded from Hype (topic 13).

## 19. 2026 changes

- [OFFICIAL] 25 Jun 2026: dislike removed from Shorts, heart icon, 2x speed, Clear Screen (topic 1).
- [OFFICIAL] 24 Jul 2026: custom Shorts thumbnails (topic 14).
- [OFFICIAL] 10 Aug 2026: YPP changes effective 1 Feb 2027 (topic 2).
- [OFFICIAL] 23 Sep 2026: Shorts series and a conversational AI editor in Shorts (topic 9).
- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] 1 Oct 2026: Shorts recommendations prioritise original content (topic 15).
- [THIRD-PARTY] January search filter for Shorts (topic 12); 24 Aug view-count change for long-form (topic 2).
- [THIRD-PARTY] The Shorts feed will start recommending posts, no date. (9to5Google, link in topic 9)
- [THIRD-PARTY, not individually verified] AIR Media-Tech's month-by-month list adds: image posts in Shorts announced 21 Jan; Reimagine AI remix 18 Mar; Shorts timer to zero for parents in Europe 20 Apr; Gemini Omni in Shorts Remix 19 May. https://air.io/en/trending/youtube-algorithm-in-2026-month-by-month-changes-that-affect-your-views

## Creator folklore

- "Post at exact hours": denied. FAQ: "Publish time is not known to impact a video's long-term performance."; Sherman 2023; Ritchie Nov 2025 (topic 5).
- "The first hour decides everything": no verbatim official denial found. Closest are the publish-time statements and outlierkit's own summary of Beaupré's Sep 2026 video, which is not a quote.
- "Deleting videos resets or helps the algorithm": denied. Beaupré on blog.youtube, 28 Mar 2024 (topic 6).
- "Delete and re-upload a weak Short": advised against. Sherman: "I would not advise that." (topic 6).
- "#shorts is required": no explicit denial found, but the official classification rule (aspect ratio, length, upload date) makes it unnecessary (topic 7).
- "New accounts need warm-up" / "new channel penalty": never confirmed; no explicit denial using those words. Beaupré describes topic-based matching for a first upload (topic 13).
- "Shadowban": no official "no such thing" statement found. Ritchie on the TubeTalk podcast (16 Feb 2026) attributes most cases to ordinary underperformance. https://tubetalk.buzzsprout.com/271511/episodes/18630508-shadow-banning-inauthentic-content-and-dislikes-with-youtube-s-rene-ritchie
- "Editing the title after publishing kills reach": denied. Changes in recommendations come from how viewers respond; "but don't change what's working." (topic 7).
- "3 Shorts a day max" / "posting too many gets you throttled": denied. Sherman: "There is nothing in our systems that's like when you hit the five video or 10 short threshold per day" (topic 4).
- "You must upload daily": denied by the FAQ (topic 4).
- "One bad video kills the channel": denied by the FAQ (topic 6).
- "Tags matter": denied. "Not important." (topic 7).
- "Shorts hurt long-form": denied. "we haven't seen evidence of Shorts negatively impacting long-form performance." (6 May 2025 blog, topic 1).
- "Trending sounds are required": denied. "they're not essential" (same blog).
- "Shorts older than 30 days are dead": neither confirmed nor denied by YouTube; third-party theory (Joos), plus the official "may tune up on the recency" line (topic 3).
- "Monetised videos get more reach": denied. "our search and recommendation system doesn't know which videos are monetizing and which are not." https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/141805?hl=en
- "Unlisted then public hurts": denied by the same FAQ.</result>

I could not open any Creator Insider video or X post directly: staff quotes from those are marked "OFFICIAL statement via third-party report". The `support.google.com/youtube/blog/...` and `/thread/...` community posts returned only navigation, so their contents are cited through press coverage.

## 1. Ranking signals

- [OFFICIAL] General recommendation inputs: "viewing behaviour, likes, dislikes, subscriptions and feedback, including from satisfaction surveys" (How YouTube Works, undated) https://www.youtube.com/howyoutubeworks/product-features/recommendations/
- [OFFICIAL] "Likes and dislikes are some of the hundreds of signals we consider for ranking." The system uses what viewers watch and don't watch, searches, likes/dislikes and "Not interested" feedback. (YouTube performance FAQ, undated) https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/141805?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL] Same FAQ, percentage viewed vs duration: YouTube uses both; relative watch time matters more for short videos, absolute for longer ones (fetch-tool paraphrase, not verbatim).
- [OFFICIAL] Shorts and long-form are ranked separately: "we've built separate recommendation systems optimized for each." (The YouTube Team, 6 May 2025) https://blog.youtube/creator-and-artist-stories/debunking-common-myths-about-youtube-shorts/
- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] Todd Sherman (Shorts product lead), Creator Insider, Aug 2023: "The audience is the algorithm."; a view should "encode for your intent of watching that thing". Thresholds are not published. https://www.searchenginejournal.com/youtube-explains-how-shorts-algorithm-works/494953/ (video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n3jsYK_-aRU)
- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] Todd Beaupré, Creator Insider, 1 Sep 2026: "We have to look at many different metrics, because no metric on its own is a good indicator of value."; "our North Star is: long-term user value." https://outlierkit.com/resources/how-youtube-recommendations-work/ (video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rHLjxrbXmmY)
- [OFFICIAL] Since 25 Jun 2026 Shorts have no dislike button and a heart replaces the thumbs-up: "we're also retiring the dislike button", in order "to more accurately tune your feed". (The YouTube Team) https://blog.youtube/news-and-events/youtube-shorts-experience-updates-features/
- [THIRD-PARTY] "Not interested" now asks for a reason; "Don't recommend this channel" remains. (ppc.land, 25 Jun 2026) https://ppc.land/youtube-shorts-removes-dislike-button-adds-heart-icon-and-2x-speed/
- [UNVERIFIED] Any official weighting of viewed vs swiped away, replays/loops, shares, comments or subscriptions from a Short. No official statement found that the "viewed vs swiped away" analytics figure is itself the ranking signal.
- [THIRD-PARTY] Social Media Today's summary lists watch time, re-watches, likes, shares and comments (its own list, not a staff quote). https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/youtube-advice-for-shorts-creators-hashtags-algorithm/691835/
- [UNVERIFIED] Paddy Galloway's "70 to 90% viewed" range appeared only in search snippets.

## 2. View counting, engaged views, YPP

- [OFFICIAL] "Starting 3/31/2025, we're updating how Shorts views are counted." "Views will count the number of times a Short starts to play or replay, with no minimum watch time requirement." The old metric is kept as "Engaged views". https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/10059070?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL] Same page: "This change will not directly impact the YouTube Partner Program (YPP) eligibility and Shorts ad revenue sharing." "They will both be based on 'Engaged Shorts views.'"
- [OFFICIAL] "For the purposes of calculating payments, YouTube uses eligible 'Engaged views'." https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/12504220?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL] Current YPP entry: "Get 1,000 subscribers with 4,000 qualified watch hours in the last 12 months" or "1,000 subscribers with 10 million qualified Shorts views in the last 90 days." https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/72851?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL] From 1 Feb 2027, new applicants need "8,000 qualified watch hours in the last 365 days" "or 20 million qualified Shorts views in the last 90 days". (The YouTube Team, 10 Aug 2026) https://blog.youtube/news-and-events/youtube-partner-program-updates-2027-new-opportunities-earn/
- [OFFICIAL] Same post: from 1 Feb 2027, Shorts revenue sharing only for "creators who have 10 million qualified Shorts views over the last 90 days"; "Channels below this threshold remain in YPP and continue earning on long-form content".
- [THIRD-PARTY] Fan funding/Shopping tier unchanged at 500 subscribers, 3 uploads in 90 days, and 3,000 watch hours or 3M Shorts views. (SEJ, 11 Aug 2026) https://www.searchenginejournal.com/youtube-updates-partner-program-terms-shorts-payout-rules/585331/ Not found on the official pages I opened.
- [THIRD-PARTY] From 24 Aug 2026 long-form public views also count from first frame; earnings stay on engaged metrics. (Engadget, 17 Aug 2026) https://engadget.com/2238611/youtube-public-view-counts-will-likely-get-higher-starting-next-week/ Official post not opened: https://support.google.com/youtube/thread/433409976?hl=en

## 3. Seed audience, long tail, freshness

- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] Sherman, Aug 2023: the algorithms "effectively find like a seed audience, find a set of people that may enjoy your video." A Short can rise then stall depending on that audience's response. (TechCrunch, 25 Aug 2023) https://techcrunch.com/2023/08/25/youtube-demystifies-the-shorts-algorithm-views-and-answers-other-creator-questions/
- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] Beaupré, 1 Sep 2026, on a first video: "we hope that we'll find some viewers who are interested, and build from there"; "if we don't, then maybe that video just won't get more impressions." https://outlierkit.com/resources/how-youtube-recommends-new-channels/
- [OFFICIAL] The only official recency statement found: "The Shorts feed, with its snackable and trendy nature, may tune up on the recency of content". (YouTube Help, undated) https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/16559651?hl=en
- [THIRD-PARTY] The "30 days" report comes from Mario Joos (retention strategist), not YouTube: from mid-September 2025, Shorts older than about 28 to 30 days lost impressions. He calls it "a carefully constructed working theory and not a confirmed fact." SEJ says YouTube has not confirmed any change. (5 Dec 2025) https://www.searchenginejournal.com/youtube-shorts-algorithm-may-now-favor-fresh-over-evergreen/562661/
- [THIRD-PARTY] Tubefilter asked Google for comment and reported none. (5 Dec 2025) https://www.tubefilter.com/2025/12/05/youtube-shorts-algorithm-change-new-uploads/
- [THIRD-PARTY, search snippet only] OverseerOS tracked 9,982 Shorts: 90.5% kept gaining views, mostly very few. https://www.overseeros.com/blog/do-youtube-shorts-get-views-after-30-days
- [OFFICIAL] The FAQ's "An old video recently took off, why?" answer is about videos in general (rising topic, new viewers bingeing), not Shorts. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/141805?hl=en
- [UNVERIFIED] No official statement that a Short is "pushed again" on a schedule, or that Shorts have a long tail.

## 4. Upload frequency, several Shorts a day

- [OFFICIAL] "growth in views across uploads is not correlated with time between uploads." Taking a break does not hurt either. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/141805?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] Sherman, Aug 2023: "There is nothing in our systems that's like when you hit the five video or 10 short threshold per day" (auto-transcript quote via https://outlierkit.com/resources/youtube-shorts-algorithm/); "that energy is probably better spent in just making a better video and fewer of them." (Social Media Today, 24 Aug 2023) https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/youtube-advice-for-shorts-creators-hashtags-algorithm/691835/
- [OFFICIAL] There is a technical daily upload cap with no published number: standard access has a "limited daily limit", higher tiers a "higher daily limit". https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/9890437?hl=en
- [UNVERIFIED] No official statement on Shorts cannibalising each other.
- [THIRD-PARTY, search snippet only] OverseerOS (18,148 Shorts): gaps of 12 to 48 hours often beat gaps under 3 hours; correlational. https://www.overseeros.com/blog/how-long-to-wait-between-youtube-shorts

## 5. Time of day

- [OFFICIAL] "Publish time is not known to impact a video's long-term performance." Posting when the audience is active may help early views. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/141805?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] Sherman, Aug 2023: "It's not something that we think about optimizing for." (via outlierkit, link above; TechCrunch notes news content as the exception.)
- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] Rene Ritchie: "Waiting 24 to 48 hours is no different than waiting 24 to 48 seconds or weeks or months. All you're doing is waiting." (SEJ, 12 Nov 2025) https://www.searchenginejournal.com/youtube-debunks-24-48-hour-upload-delay-recommendation/560613/ (video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Zf7tOh6y39o)
- [OFFICIAL] "Shorts don't trigger notifications on upload". (Rene's Top Five, 28 Mar 2024) https://blog.youtube/culture-and-trends/renes-top-five-on-youtube-march-28-2024-edition/

## 6. Deleting, re-uploading, poor performers

- [OFFICIAL] Beaupré, quoted on YouTube's blog: "Don't delete videos unless you have a very, very good reason." "When you delete a video, you delete your channel's connection to the audience that watched that video." (28 Mar 2024) https://blog.youtube/culture-and-trends/renes-top-five-on-youtube-march-28-2024-edition/
- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] Sherman on delete-and-repost: "I would not advise that." "there's also a risk that it gets seen as spam in our systems." (Social Media Today, 24 Aug 2023, link above)
- [OFFICIAL] An underperforming video does not hurt the channel by itself: "What matters is how viewers reply to each video when it's recommended to them." https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/141805?hl=en

## 7. Title, description, hashtags, category, language, tags

- [OFFICIAL] Tags: "Not important." (mainly for spelling variants). Changing title/thumbnail can help "but don't change what's working." https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/141805?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL] Hashtags: "Hashtags also allow viewers and listeners to find related content via search." "If a video or playlist has more than 60 hashtags, we'll ignore each hashtag". No mention of #shorts. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/6390658?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL] #shorts is not needed for classification: uploads from 15 Oct 2024 "with a square or vertical aspect ratio up to three minutes in length will be categorized as Shorts". https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/15424877?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] Sherman on hashtags: sometimes tied to events, "Other times they're focused on topics, and I think in both those cases, creators should consider using them." (Social Media Today, link above)
- [OFFICIAL] Video language setting: "It's also used to help viewers find videos in their language." https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/6304325?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] With no behavioural data, the system uses "the user's topical preferences and what we understand about what this video is about" (Beaupré, 1 Sep 2026, via outlierkit, link in topic 3).
- [UNVERIFIED] No official statement found on the category field affecting Shorts ranking.

## 8. Captions and dubbing

- [OFFICIAL] Automatic dubbing: "This feature is enabled by default for eligible creators." "When you upload a new video, dubs will be automatically generated." Not generated when there is little speech or the video exceeds 120 minutes. The page does not mention Shorts. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/15569972?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL] "Auto dubbing is available in 27 languages."; "having your videos dubbed has no negative impact on viewer discovery." (Rene Ritchie, 15 May 2026) https://blog.youtube/creator-and-artist-stories/youtube-auto-dubbing-explained/
- [OFFICIAL via third-party report] "all new content, both shorts and VODs, will be automatically dubbed upon upload" (Social Media Today, 24 Jun 2025) https://www.socialmediatoday.com/news/youtube-expands-auto-dubbing-dream-screen-inspiration-tab/751554/
- [OFFICIAL] Manual multi-language audio covers Shorts ("to a single video or Short") but is "currently available to creators with access to Advanced features." Translated titles/descriptions are used by search. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13338784?hl=en
- [UNVERIFIED] Whether a brand-new, unverified channel gets auto-dubbing on Shorts; any official statement on captions affecting Shorts reach.

## 9. Playlists, series, related video

- [OFFICIAL] Shorts can be added to playlists from the Short's watch page; reordering "isn't available for playlists that only contain YouTube Shorts." https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/57792?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL] Made on YouTube 2026 recap (23 Sep 2026) mentions "structured Shorts series", with no details. https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/youtube/made-on-youtube-updates-2026/
- [THIRD-PARTY] Shorts series let creators "organize their Shorts into seasons and episodes", "rolling out starting today". (9to5Google, 23 Sep 2026) https://9to5google.com/2026/09/23/made-on-youtube-2026/ No official help page with steps found.
- [OFFICIAL] Related video: "A related video allows you to showcase your Videos, Shorts, and Live in the Shorts player." Requires advanced feature access, is set in YouTube Studio on the web, and the target must be public or unlisted. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/14075157?hl=en

## 10. Pinned comments and links

- [OFFICIAL] "To reduce spam and scam attempts, URLs placed in YouTube Shorts comments and Shorts descriptions are non-clickable." The related-video link is clickable; channel profile links allow up to 14 links. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13748639?hl=en
- [THIRD-PARTY] Effective date 31 Aug 2023. (Tubefilter, 10 Aug 2023) https://tubefilter.com/2023/08/10/youtube-shorts-comments-spam/ The official page shows no date.
- [OFFICIAL] Pinned comments are listed under advanced features, which a new channel gets through channel history or ID/video verification. Tier placement is as read by the fetch tool; check the live table. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/9890437?hl=en

## 11. Shorts up to 3 minutes

- [OFFICIAL] Applies to uploads from "October 15, 2024", square or vertical, up to three minutes. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/15424877?hl=en
- [OFFICIAL] Shorts over one minute "with an active copyright claim of any type, including manual claims, will be blocked globally on YouTube." Blocked Shorts "will not be playable or recommended". Music: "You can use most songs for up to 90 seconds in a 3 minute Short." (same page)
- [OFFICIAL] "Shorts longer than one minute that have an active copyright claim, regardless of the policy, will be blocked on YouTube." https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/6013276?hl=en
- [UNVERIFIED] No official statement found that 1 to 3 minute Shorts are recommended differently from shorter ones. A vidIQ video reportedly claimed worse distribution (search snippet only).

## 12. Search

- [THIRD-PARTY] January 2026: a "Shorts" option was added to the search Type filter, and the duration bracket now starts at three minutes.
